name: wps-hide-login
notes: Adapter-authoring probe 2026-08-22: inspected the official WordPress.org WPS Hide Login 1.9.19 artifact (SHA-256 34e99ee6032f5863b278aef690ebbfdb00290beb4eacbdae3ab931eb719b3a58). The range is one patch wide and the settings are security-sensitive, so widening requires a new request-routing exercise.

classes/plugin.php register_settings(), new_login_slug(), and new_redirect_slug() identify whl_page and whl_redirect_admin as the two current single-site settings. Both are sanitized route slugs, read directly for request routing, and are portable authored choices rather than URLs, ids, or credentials. whl_redirect is a deleted legacy activation-redirect marker.

The settings-screen and network-save paths call flush_rewrite_rules(true), but exact 1.9.19 registers no rewrite rule: plugins_loaded() and wp_loaded() read whl_page/whl_redirect_admin for every request, and the URL filters read the same options. The isolated conformance matrix preserves a deliberately stale target rewrite_rules byte set across raw option apply while proving custom GET/POST/lost-password/authenticated login, direct and URL-encoded old-login refusal, anonymous/admin routing, public routing, uninstall/reinstall recovery, and pretty/plain permalink behavior. Because the plugin has no separate route projection to repair, no provider is declared. The network defaults remain outside Duo's multisite-refusing v1 contract.

The certified request contract uses non-empty ASCII slugs normalized by WordPress's sanitize_title_with_dashes(), including its 200-byte maximum; absence exercises the plugin's native login/404 fallbacks. The evidence also pins traversal, path-separator, wp-login, empty, and percent-encoded Unicode sanitizer outputs so a future artifact cannot silently change the data boundary. Configuration quality remains the plugin/operator's concern: Duo reproduces the exact authored bytes and does not invent a second settings validator.
